subject: Business Models
title: Marquee Users
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Marquee Users.

hook.text: Apple paid developers millions to create exclusive iPhone apps at launch. Quality over quantity.

buildup.text: Marquee users are high-profile early adopters whose presence alone attracts the masses.

discovery.text: Clubhouse gave early access to celebrities like Elon Musk. His presence drew millions of signups.

twist.text: Marquee users can also leave loudly. When celebrities abandoned Clubhouse, growth cratered.

climax.text: Marquee users accelerate the chicken-and-egg solution but create fragile dependence on individuals.

punchline.text: One famous user draws millions. But fame is fleeting.

quiz.question: What risk do marquee users create for platforms?

details.summary: Marquee users are high-profile participants whose presence on a platform attracts large numbers of other users. Celebrities on Twitter, popular streamers on Twitch, and anchor tenants in shopping malls all serve as demand magnets that accelerate platform growth disproportionately.
details.whyItMatters: A single marquee user can attract millions of followers. Platforms that secure key marquee users early gain an outsized growth advantage. This strategy is central to content platforms, marketplaces, and gaming ecosystems.
takeaways: Marquee users attract disproportionately large numbers of other participants
Platforms often pay premium incentives to secure high-profile early users
Losing marquee users can trigger cascading departures of their followers

faq.question: How do platforms attract and retain marquee users?
faq.answer: Revenue sharing deals, exclusive contracts, custom features, priority support, and creative tools tailored to their needs. YouTube pays top creators through its Partner Program. Spotify pays exclusive podcast deals. Twitch offers top streamers custom subscription terms.

faq.question: What risks come with depending on marquee users?
faq.answer: Platform dependence on a few stars creates concentration risk. If marquee users leave for a competing platform, they can take millions of followers. This gives marquee users enormous bargaining power and makes platforms vulnerable to competitive poaching.
